transcription.tex: [STEP 2009 Q8 Edited] If equation of the circle \(C\) is \({\left(x-2t\right)}^{2}+{\left(y-t\right)}^{2}={t}^{2}\), where \(t\) is a positive number, it can be shown that \(C\) touches the line \(y=0\) as well as the line \(3y=4x\).\par Find the equation of the incircle of the triangle formed by the lines \(y=0\), \(3y=4x\) and \(4y+3x=15\).\par Note: The incircle of a triangle is the circle, lying totally inside the triangle, that touches all three sides.
\text{Given: the family \((x-2t)^2+(y-t)^2=t^2\), t>0, touches the first two lines. The incircle lies entirely inside the triangle.}
\text{Tangency to y=0 gives centre (h,t) and radius t>0. For a centre inside the triangle, its distance to \(4x-3y=0\) gives\[\frac{4h-3t}{5}=t\Rightarrow h=2t\]}
\text{The distance from (2t,t) to \(3x+4y=15\) is t. Inside the triangle,\[\frac{15-10t}{5}=t\Rightarrow t=1\]}
